editorial.headline: Sound Recording: Nationally Open, Blocked for PMA Registration in Bali
editorial.standfirst: Sound-recording work is nationally open to full foreign ownership, but Bali’s permanent risk-based moratorium blocks PMA registration for it.
editorial.body:
A foreign investor cannot register this sound-recording activity in Bali today. That is the practical effect of Bali’s island-wide, permanent moratorium on PMA registrations for activities assessed as Low or Medium-Low risk. For this activity, the Bali record identifies every scope at the Besar scale as Low or Medium-Low risk. The moratorium is recorded as applying from May 13, 2026, so the national position and Bali’s registration reality must be read separately from the outset.

At its core, the activity concerns making original master sound recordings. It also covers recording services, including pre-recorded, non-live radio programmes, audio podcasts, and audio for films, television, books, and other media. Converting sound recordings into audio-streaming formats also sits within the scope. This is work concerned with producing and recording sound, then preparing it for streaming; it does not extend to distributing moving-image or comparable audiovisual works, nor to publishing software.

Registration is open across the stated operating scales: Mikro, Kecil, Menengah, and Besar. Nationally, its foreign-investment status is TERBUKA, with a maximum foreign ownership of 100 per cent. In plain terms, the national record permits full foreign ownership for this activity. That national openness, however, is not a promise of registration in every location. In Bali, the provincial rule takes effect independently of the national ownership ceiling.

That distinction is the essential one. Bali’s bar arises from the recorded OSS risk position at the Besar scale and the province’s rule blocking all Low and Medium-Low risk KBLI for PMA. It is not a national closure of foreign participation. Nationally, the activity is open to up to full foreign ownership; in Bali, it is blocked for PMA registration under the permanent moratorium. For a founder considering Bali, that is the decisive answer.
editorial.pullQuote: Nationally open to full foreign ownership, this activity is nevertheless barred from PMA registration in Bali.
